title: Erdős #100 OQ: Distance Set Diameter Growth Rate
description: Is the minimum diameter of n-point integer distance sets Θ(n) (linear) or Θ(n/log n)?

meta.author: Open problem

mathlibDependencies.description: Eventually n ≥ N for the asymptotic statements

originalContributions: Proved strong conjecture implies linear lower bound with c = 1/2
Proved Guth-Katz bound cn/log n is strictly sublinear (the gap is exactly log n)
meta.assumptions: Inherits axioms from Erdos100Problem.lean (guthKatz_distinct_distances, piepmeyer_construction, kanold_bound, erdos_anning_theorem) via import.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős and Anning (1945) proved that infinitely many collinear points cannot all have integer pairwise distances unless they are collinear. The question of how the minimum diameter of n-point integer distance sets grows with n remains open, with the best known bound of cn/log n following from Guth-Katz (2015).
overview.problemStatement: Is the minimum diameter of n-point integer distance sets Θ(n) (linear growth) or Θ(n/log n) (matching the current best bound from Guth-Katz)?
overview.text: The gap between the conjectured linear bound and the proven n/log n bound is exactly a factor of log n.
overview.proofStrategy: Two results are formalized: (1) the strong conjecture (diam ≥ n-1) implies a linear lower bound with c = 1/2, via simple arithmetic; (2) the Guth-Katz bound cn/log n is eventually strictly less than cn, quantifying the gap.
keyInsights: The strong conjecture (diam ≥ n-1) immediately implies a linear bound via n-1 ≥ n/2
The current best bound cn/log n differs from the conjectured cn by exactly one log factor
The kanold_bound axiom in the parent file is logically redundant — it follows from the proved diam_ge_n_over_log_n

conclusion.summary: Formalizes two results about the gap between known (n/log n) and conjectured (n) diameter bounds for integer distance sets.
openQuestions: Can the log n factor be removed from the Guth-Katz bound to achieve linear growth?
Is kanold_bound provable from the existing theorems (eliminating a redundant axiom)?

crossReferences.relationship: Open question derived from parent problem

mainTheorems.name: strong_implies_half_linear
mainTheorems.description: Strong conjecture implies diam ≥ n/2 for every n-point integer distance set

mainTheorems.name: gk_bound_strictly_sublinear
mainTheorems.description: For any c > 0, cn/log n < cn eventually (the gap is exactly log n)
